title: Cold-chain account users, roles and sign-in settings
source_system: Cold-chain vendor portal (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: One user account, the owner's, with the administrator role; the role catalog has administrator and view-only roles, and only the administrator can change alarm set points and alert contacts; sign-in by password only, with MFA offered and turned off; no record of a user list review

title: Cold-chain sensor, alert and gateway settings
source_system: Cold-chain vendor portal (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: 5 wireless temperature sensors (carcass cooler 2, freezer 2, processing room 1) report through one gateway; alarm set points are 38 F for the carcass cooler and 10 F for the freezer; alerts go by text message and app notification to one contact, the owner's phone; no second contact is set; the vendor's "gateway offline" notice is turned off; the gateway connects over the shop Wi-Fi; the anomaly alert feature is on and flags unusual temperature patterns for the owner to review

title: Cold-chain activity log and export history
source_system: Cold-chain vendor portal (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: The activity log records sign-ins, set point changes, alert contact changes and alert acknowledgments by user, and can be filtered and exported; temperature history can be exported as a spreadsheet; the account shows no log review, log export or history export

title: Cold-chain vendor subscription terms and report request
source_system: Cold-chain vendor portal (SYS-01); email inbox (SYS-05)
what_it_shows: Click-through subscription terms accepted at sign-up; the portal offers a SOC 2 Type 2 report on request; the account's request history shows no earlier request for the report; the owner requested it on 2026-07-20

title: Cold-chain vendor SOC 2 Type 2 report
source_system: Cold-chain vendor (provided on request)
what_it_shows: Type 2 report on the Security and Availability categories for the 12 months ending 2026-03-31, unmodified opinion; one exception (a departed vendor employee's access removed 9 days late, 1 of 25 sampled) reported as remediated; the system description states encrypted, integrity-checked backups stored in a separate location, encryption at rest and in transit, and annual platform recovery tests; the gateway buffers readings for up to 12 hours without internet and uploads them later, but cannot send alerts while offline; gateway hardware is covered only for firmware delivery; cloud hosting and the text-message delivery service are carved-out subservice organizations; MFA is offered to customer users; customers are told of security incidents through the account email; complementary user entity controls: protect credentials and enable MFA, maintain alert contacts and set points, keep gateways powered and connected, review activity reports, and report suspected compromise

title: Smokehouse app account and controller settings
source_system: Smokehouse manufacturer cloud app (SYS-02)
what_it_shows: The app account signs in with a password only, and the app offers no MFA; remote monitoring, remote start and stop, and remote program editing are on; the controller stores 10 cook programs (stages, temperatures, times); no copy of the programs is kept outside the controller and the app; the controller connects over the shop Wi-Fi

title: Smokehouse app terms, as accepted
source_system: Smokehouse manufacturer website; app (SYS-02)
what_it_shows: Click-through app terms accepted when the controller was set up; the owner has no copy of them and no notes from reading them; the current terms were downloaded at intake

title: Laptop settings and contents review
source_system: Shop laptop settings screens (SYS-03)
what_it_shows: One user account, with administrator rights, used for daily shop work and not shared with family; full-disk encryption on (on by default); automatic OS updates on and current; built-in antivirus on, with real-time protection and automatic updates; host firewall on; no backup set up; the browser stores the passwords for every shop account, and its password check flags the cold-chain and smokehouse app passwords as the same; label software drives the scale and label printer over USB; the label templates and the cure calculation sheet are stored only on the laptop; a synced copy of the custom records spreadsheet and cut-sheet PDFs; the browser history includes the public AI chatbot

title: Phone settings review
source_system: Phone settings screens (SYS-06)
what_it_shows: Passcode and device encryption on; automatic updates on; holds the cold-chain and smokehouse apps, the card reader app, the bank app and email; receives the email account's text-message codes; the only device registered for cold-chain alerts, with the alert history; kill sheet photos from the slaughter operator and customer texts in the message threads

title: Scale and label printer check
source_system: Scale and label printer; label software on the laptop (SYS-04)
what_it_shows: A test label printed from the template shows "Not for Sale" in lettering at least 3/8 inch high, with the owner's name and the cut; a roll of preprinted "Not for Sale" labels is kept at the scale

title: Email and file account security page and storage review
source_system: Consumer email and file account (SYS-05)
what_it_shows: Consumer plan in the owner's name, also used for personal mail; MFA by text message, turned on in 2024 at the provider's prompt; the provider keeps a sign-in history, with no record of a review; no file version history on this plan and no backup set up; file storage holds the custom records spreadsheet (2024 to 2026), cut sheets, kill sheet photos and booking form submissions; the tax preparer has a shared link to an accounting export folder

title: Custom records spreadsheet review
source_system: Custom records spreadsheet in the file account (SYS-05)
what_it_shows: One spreadsheet for 2024 to 2026, synced to the laptop; about 640 livestock and product owners, each share owner a separate record, with names, street addresses, phone numbers and email addresses, nearly all at Florida addresses; entries for about 180 beef, 260 hogs, and 40 lambs and goats a year, each with owner, species, carcass number, hanging weight and finished weight; pickup dates are blank for the 2024 entries; entries are typed from kill sheet photos and cut sheets; no Social Security, driver license or financial account numbers; the file shows no earlier versions

title: Booking form admin settings and submissions
source_system: Booking form vendor admin console (SYS-07)
what_it_shows: The admin account signs in with a password only, with MFA offered and turned off; customers have no accounts; submissions (processing date requests and cut sheets with names, addresses, phone numbers and emails) are kept in the vendor account and emailed to the owner's mailbox; the service runs under click-through terms

title: Vendor account contact settings
source_system: Account settings in SYS-01, SYS-02, SYS-05, SYS-07, SYS-08 and SYS-10
what_it_shows: Every vendor account lists the owner's personal email address as its only contact for notices; no separate shop security contact is registered with any vendor

title: Accounting, banking and card reader settings
source_system: Accounting SaaS, online banking and card reader app (SYS-08)
what_it_shows: Accounting SaaS: MFA on (vendor default for new accounts); invoices carry customer names. Online banking: a one-time code is required before a new payee is added. Card reader: processor-managed, paired with the phone, and encrypts card data at the reader; card numbers are not stored on or passed through shop-managed systems; some customers pay by check

title: Signed agreements folder
source_system: Signed agreements folder (paper and file account)
what_it_shows: Card processor merchant agreement, which requires the shop to protect card data and report suspected compromise of the reader (PCI DSS reaches the shop through these terms); tax preparer engagement letter; refrigeration contractor service terms with a 24-hour emergency line; no written agreement with the slaughter operator, a neighboring custom processor, or any provider of emergency cooler space or standby power; no federal contract

title: Processing fee report, 2025 and 2026 to date
source_system: Accounting SaaS reporting (SYS-08)
what_it_shows: Processing fees of about $180,000 in 2025, about $3,500 a week in the October to December busy season and less in summer; invoices are for processing fees only, with no meat sales

title: 2025 Schedule C (Form 1040)
source_system: Owner's tax files (prepared by the tax preparer)
what_it_shows: Gross receipts of about $180,000 in processing fees; no wages paid; the business is a sole proprietorship with no employees; prepared from accounting SaaS exports

title: Router and Wi-Fi settings
source_system: Internet provider router admin page (SYS-09)
what_it_shows: The router is supplied by the internet provider and was installed several years ago; one network carries the laptop, phone, cold-chain gateway, smokehouse controller and customers' phones, as the connected-device list shows; no guest network is set up; the router firewall is on and no port is forwarded; the admin password in use is the one printed on the router label; the update history lists no firmware update since installation

title: Shop walk-through
source_system: Shop building (observation)
what_it_shows: A 2,000-square-foot shop building on the owner's rural inland homestead, next to the house; the shop is locked with a key when the owner is away; curing agents are in a locked cabinet, the owner holds the only key, and each container is marked with its nitrite content; customers stay at the pickup counter; old paper cut sheets and kill sheet printouts sit in open boxes behind the pickup counter; dial thermometers in both walk-ins and a paper log with readings at opening and closing; the gateway and router are plugged into wall outlets with no battery backup; two packaged condensing units and no standby generator or transfer switch; cleaning chemicals stored apart from product; bones and trim in marked inedible containers; the cure supplier's printed chart in the processing room; no written outage, storm or cooler emergency procedure posted; the owner states that customers waiting at pickup are given the Wi-Fi password when they ask

title: Kill sheet photos and carcass intake records
source_system: Phone message threads (SYS-06); custom records (SYS-05)
what_it_shows: Kill sheet photos texted by the mobile slaughter operator list the livestock owner, species, carcass number and hot weight for each delivery; every carcass recorded for 2024 to 2026 is beef, pork, lamb or goat, delivered tagged with the owner's name; no wild game appears

title: FSIS custom exempt review record, March 2026
source_system: Paper files (copy left at the FSIS review)
what_it_shows: FSIS review of the custom exempt operation in March 2026, with no noncompliance noted; the records examined include the custom records, which the owner states were shown on the laptop

title: Cure calculation sheet and batch sheets
source_system: Shop laptop (SYS-03); paper batch sheets
what_it_shows: The cure calculation sheet is a laptop spreadsheet with no version history or change record; the 2026 batch sheets record cure and brine amounts for bacon, ham and smoked sausage batches with no note of how each amount was calculated or checked

title: Public chatbot account history and settings
source_system: Public generative AI chatbot (free consumer account, SYS-10)
what_it_shows: Free consumer account in the owner's name, used from the laptop browser and the phone since January 2026; about 30 conversations, mostly scaling cure and brine amounts for bacon, ham and smoked sausage to customer batch weights, and drafts of customer texts, some with a first name and pickup time; 12 answers with cure amounts are saved; the setting that lets the vendor use conversations to improve its service is on

title: Public chatbot terms of use, as accepted
source_system: Chatbot vendor website
what_it_shows: Consumer terms, accepted at sign-up in January 2026, let the vendor use inputs to improve its service

title: Bank and card statements, 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30
source_system: Business bank account and card statements
what_it_shows: Recurring payments to the cold-chain monitoring vendor, the booking form vendor, the consumer email and file plan, the accounting SaaS vendor, the internet provider and the phone carrier; payments to the label software vendor, the refrigeration contractor, the cure and casing suppliers, the tax preparer, and the IT technician by the hour; the business liability insurance premium; card processor deposits and fees; no payment to the chatbot vendor and no payment for a cyber insurance policy

title: Vendor invoices and correspondence
source_system: Email inbox (SYS-05)
what_it_shows: Refrigeration contractor invoices for service on the two condensing units, showing its 24-hour emergency line; IT technician invoices billed by the hour for laptop, phone and router help, with no recurring service or standing access; invoices from established cure, spice and casing suppliers; a 2023 sign-up email for a label software trial account, with no cancellation or closing email; vendor notices arrive mixed with personal mail

title: Business liability policy declarations
source_system: Insurance agent portal
what_it_shows: Business liability policy in force for 2026; the declarations page lists no cyber coverage or endorsement; the full policy form was requested from the agent

title: Search of the owner's files for security documents
source_system: Laptop; file account; email account; paper files
what_it_shows: Not found: a written security policy or procedure, a risk assessment or risk tolerance statement, a security role designation, an incident plan, incident log or contact list, a breach notice procedure, a written cold-chain outage, storm or cooler emergency procedure, a recovery or contingency plan, a reciprocal or emergency cooler space agreement, a retention or disposal rule, a vendor list or vendor review record, a device list, a network diagram, an AI use rule, printed cook programs, or a security course certificate or reminder subscription; no copy of the custom records, cook programs, cure sheet or label templates outside where they are kept; no FDA food facility registration

title: BIA self-review worksheet
source_system: Owner-operator's written BIA worksheet, reviewed with the IT technician
what_it_shows: For each of the five business functions, the owner's account of the systems, vendors and season involved, the manual workaround, and the longest outage and data loss the function can tolerate; a closed walk-in holds temperature for only a few hours without power or a working unit; one carcass cooler can hold more than $10,000 of customers' beef; the slaughter operator delivers on fixed days; the owner is the only person who performs each function and the only alert recipient

title: Risk walk-through of the shop, devices and SaaS accounts
source_system: Walk-through with the IT technician
what_it_shows: Where shop data and credentials sit day to day (the laptop browser, the file account, kill sheet photos on the phone, paper in the shop); who can change alarm set points, alert contacts and cook programs; the single alert path from sensor to gateway to vendor cloud to one phone; the laptop and phone travel between the shop, the house and the truck; payment requests and changes arrive by email; when a storm is forecast the owner stops taking carcasses, which is not written down

title: Gap analysis self-review
source_system: Owner-operator's written answers to the CSF 2.0, 9 CFR and Fla. Stat. 501.171 questions, checked on screen with the IT technician
what_it_shows: Stakeholders' security expectations are not written down; there were no security objectives, risk tolerance or risk response approach; spoilage and storm risks are managed by habit, and cyber risks were never considered alongside them; there is no security budget; vendors were chosen on price and features, and the chatbot and smokehouse app terms were not read before use; supplier security was never considered; no threat information is received; software comes from official stores and vendor sites, and device firmware has never been checked; changes were made without thought for risk (remote program editing was turned on at setup); there were no tests or exercises; lessons from past cooler alarms were never written down; alerts are acknowledged without further analysis; incidents would be handled as they arise; the owner did not know the shop is a covered entity under Fla. Stat. 501.171; there is no plan for telling livestock owners about held or lost product; cure amounts are compared with the supplier's chart by habit, not on paper; the shop is cleaned daily, and the grinder cleaning time is noted on each customer's cut sheet; the shop publishes and develops no software; no identity provider or federated sign-in is used; internet and SaaS capacity is ample for five sensors and one laptop

title: Saved chatbot cure answers check
source_system: Public chatbot account (SYS-10); cure supplier's printed chart
what_it_shows: 12 saved chatbot answers compared with the cure supplier's printed chart: 11 matched, and 1 (a brine for 40 lb of ham) gave a cure amount about 25% higher than the chart; the owner states that this number looked high at the time and the chart value was used for that batch; earlier checks were not written down

title: Control assessment: Activity review self-review
source_system: Cold-chain activity log; email sign-in history; owner self-review
what_it_shows: The cold-chain activity log and the email sign-in history have never been reviewed; the log records set point and alert contact changes that no one looks at; no process exists to act on review results or to review more often in the busy season or after an incident

title: Control assessment: Backup review
source_system: Cold-chain vendor SOC 2 report; file account settings; laptop and smokehouse controller review; owner self-review
what_it_shows: The cold-chain vendor encrypts its backups, checks their integrity and stores them in a separate location (SOC 2 report); the custom records spreadsheet, cut sheets and kill sheet photos have no backup or version history; the cook programs, label templates and cure sheet have no backup; security documents are kept only in the consumer file account with no versioning

title: Control assessment: MFA sign-in test
source_system: Cold-chain, smokehouse, email, booking form and accounting account security pages; sign-in tests from a new browser
what_it_shows: Email (text message) and accounting required a second factor; the cold-chain account and the booking form admin signed in with a password only; the smokehouse app offers no MFA

title: Control assessment: Password and default credential test
source_system: Laptop browser password store (count only); router admin page and smokehouse controller panel sign-in tests; account recovery settings; owner self-review
what_it_shows: The router admin page and the smokehouse controller panel accepted their factory default credentials, and the owner changed both the same day; the cold-chain and smokehouse accounts share an 11-character word and number password that the owner also used on a personal shopping account; the laptop browser stores every shop password and shows them after the device password; no steps exist for a lost or compromised password, and no rule to change a password after a vendor breach notice or suspected exposure; cold-chain recovery codes were never saved; no written rules for protecting passwords; the laptop is encrypted and the phone is protected by passcode and encryption; the owner set up every account personally and issues no credentials to anyone else; no group or role accounts exist

title: Control assessment: Incident reporting self-review
source_system: Contact lists; vendor account notification settings; owner self-review
what_it_shows: No reporting time is defined; vendor breach notices go to the personal mailbox; there is no list of whom to notify (IT technician, counsel, refrigeration contractor, Florida Department of Legal Affairs)

title: Control assessment: Risk assessment review
source_system: P01 risk register; P05 BIA; owner self-review
what_it_shows: The 2026 risk assessment identifies 15 threat events with sources and vulnerabilities; it rates likelihood and impact with Tables G-5 and I-2, including harm to customers' product, and rates the impact of disclosing customers' names and addresses (R-008); it takes its business view from the BIA and is documented in the register and report; results were shared with the IT technician; no review frequency or update trigger was defined at the time of assessment

title: Control assessment: Vendor review
source_system: Vendor terms; cold-chain vendor SOC 2 report (reviewed 2026-07-30); vendor account settings; owner self-review
what_it_shows: No security requirements are set for any vendor, and no required vendor controls (for example an MFA option or breach notice) are defined; the chatbot's consumer terms allow use of inputs to improve its service; the smokehouse app terms had not been read; no vendor list or oversight steps are documented; the cold-chain vendor's SOC 2 report lists the customer's responsibilities; only the cold-chain vendor has been reviewed, once

title: Control assessment: Network test
source_system: Router settings and connected-device list; reachability test from a phone on the shop Wi-Fi; port check from outside the network
what_it_shows: A phone on the shop Wi-Fi reached the router admin page and the smokehouse controller; the laptop, gateway, smokehouse controller and customers' phones share one network, with no guest network and no monitoring between them; nobody looks at the router's connected-device list or logs; the router blocks unsolicited inbound connections and the port check found no forwarded port; all external connections go through the router, with no cellular modem or other path

title: Control assessment: Malicious code protection test
source_system: Antivirus status page; standard antivirus test file downloaded
what_it_shows: The built-in antivirus detected the test file on download, quarantined and removed it, and showed an alert on the laptop; signature updates install automatically (last update the same day); scheduled scans and real-time protection for downloads and attachments are on; the owner checks the quarantine list when alerted; no false positives recorded
